patient_actor_hidden.History: The patient has been experiencing generalized fatigue and easy bruising for 3 weeks. Over the past week, she has developed a fever and severe leg pain that wakes her up at night.

Secondary_Symptoms: Severe leg pain that disturbs sleep

patient_actor_hidden.Social_History: Attends preschool. Lives with parents and one younger sibling.
patient_actor_hidden.Review_of_Systems: Positive for fever, bruising, and bone pain. Denies cough, vomiting, diarrhea, rash, or urinary symptoms.

objective_for_doctor: Evaluate and manage a pediatric patient presenting with a 3-week history of generalized fatigue, easy bruising, fever, and severe leg pain.

turns.content: Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—can you tell me your age, and whether the bruising is new/worsening along with fevers over the past 3 weeks? Patient: I’m 6 years old, and the bruising and fevers have definitely gotten worse. Doctor: Any bone pain worse at night or swelling near joints, and have you noticed shortness of breath, pale skin, or frequent infections?

Patient: I’m 6 years old, the bruising and fevers have gotten worse, and I’ve had severe leg pain that wakes me up at night with no swelling near my joints. I don’t think I’ve been short of breath, and I haven’t had frequent infections or rash.

Doctor: I’m concerned about a serious blood/bone marrow problem—can you ask if the leg pain is one-sided or both legs, and whether you’ve had any gum bleeding, nosebleeds, or tiny red/purple spots (petechiae)? Also, have you lost weight or had bone pain in other places besides the legs? Doctor: REQUEST TEST: CBC_with_differential, Peripheral_blood_smear, Coagulation_panel_(PT/INR, aPTT), LDH, Uric_acid, Comprehensive_metabolic_panel, Blood_culture Doctor: If possible, please get a STAT exam: check vitals, pallor, lymph nodes, hepatosplenomegaly, and perform a focused skin exam for petechiae/bruising distribution.

RESULTS: - Vitals: Temperature 38.3°C (100.9°F); Heart rate 120/min; Respiratory rate 30/min - General exam: Pale, appears fatigued; cervical and axillary lymphadenopathy present - Abdominal exam: Liver palpable 3 cm below right costal margin; spleen palpable 2 cm below left costal margin; abdomen soft and nontender - CBC: Hemoglobin 10.1 g/dL (low); Leukocyte count 63,000/mm3 (high); Platelet count 27,000/mm3 (low) - Bone marrow aspirate: Predominantly immature cells positive for CD10, CD19, and TdT - (Requested additional tests not provided in provided data): CBC with differential (not specified beyond leukocyte count), peripheral blood smear, coagulation panel (PT/INR, aPTT), LDH, uric acid, comprehensive

Doctor: With your high white count (63,000), low hemoglobin, and very low platelets plus bruising/fever, and your marrow showing immature cells that are TdT-positive with CD10 and CD19, the most likely diagnosis is acute lymphoblastic leukemia—do you have any of the coagulation test results (PT/INR, aPTT) to confirm bleeding risk, and has a neurologic symptom like headache or vomiting occurred? Doctor: DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL), B-cell precursor (TdT+, CD10+, CD19+)
